author: thechecker111
quote:
GTA VI is feminist woke slop disguised as a crime simulator.

GTA used to be funny, outrageous, and unapologetically criminal. Now it's a tedious 9-to-5 chore simulator with a mandatory simping dating sim attached.

Jason is a soulless golem whose entire existence revolves around pleasing Lucia, one of the most unlikeable characters Rockstar has ever written. She's stupid, manipulative, irresponsible, and constantly flirts with other men.

She ghosted Jason, secretly gave birth to his child, then left the baby unattended in a café while robbing a store, which landed her in prison. And now Jason is expected to do absolutely everything for her.

Fix her roof, repair her stairs, paint her bedroom, buy her clothes and jewelry, get groceries, fix her car, pick her up from community service, defend her to her probation officer, meditate and do yoga with her, shop for a baby crib, assemble IKEA furniture, watch TV together, and massage her feet. And what exactly does Jason get in return? Practically nothing.

The most absurd moment was when I had to meet Lucia's pregnant friend outside prison and PRESS R2 TO FEEL HER BABY BUMP. IN A GTA GAME!

Meanwhile, the series' traditional male fantasies have been stripped away. Having multiple girlfriends or visiting prostitutes, features that existed in previous GTA games, are gone. Jason is forced into a monogamous relationship with Lucia, although apparently that expectation only applies to him. Lucia constantly flirts with other men, and the game even hints at infidelity.

And the endless chores! You have to refuel your car, drink protein shakes, work out regularly or lose muscle mass, feed your pet snake, maintain your house and vehicle, pick Lucia up from work, and keep contributing to your child's savings account.

I think the only thing Rockstar forgot was making us file our tax returns.

Countless new mechanics are being praised by professional critics as "immersive," when most of them simply make the game more tedious.

Rockstar also copied heavily from Red Dead Redemption 2. You can greet or antagonize NPCs, inspect animals and collect records of inspected species, and perform endless mundane chores. These mechanics made sense in a cowboy game set in the 19th century. In a game set in 2026, they're just digital repetitions of the boring responsibilities I already have in real life.

Even the morality system feels imported from RDR2. Kill too many NPCs and you get bad karma. Spare them and receive good-boy points. What a bizarre design decision for a franchise that's fundamentally supposed to be a crime simulator.

I remember GTA: San Andreas, where causing destruction and behaving like a dangerous gangster could increase your status and respect. Now the opposite is true.

The police are another problem. Practically every illegal action immediately attracts law enforcement. Getting arrested can cost you your mission progress and rewards, so you think twice before running over an NPC on your way home. Instead, you obediently drive back, follow the rules, and avoid causing trouble.

It's like buying a racing game that tells you racing is illegal and makes you wash cars instead.

And almost nobody among the professional critics seems interested in discussing what the game has taken away from the series.

GTA VI has turned a crime sandbox into a tedious 9-to-5 chore simulator with mandatory simping.
